PUSH="git push"
p() {
    local cmd="$1" cwd="${2:-$W}" out rc

}
echo "--- ref gate, want deny ---"
for c in "git -c core.pager=cat $PUSH origin main" "git --no-pager $PUSH origin main" \
         "git -p $PUSH origin main" "git --literal-pathspecs $PUSH origin main" \
         "git -c a=b --no-pager $PUSH origin main" "$PUSH origin +main" \
         "$PUSH origin +refs/heads/main" "$PUSH origin HEAD:main" \
         'git \"push\" origin main' "GIT_TRACE=1 $PUSH origin main" \
         "cd foo && $PUSH origin main"; do
    printf '%-52s %s\n' "$c" "$(p "$c")"
done
echo "--- branch gate (bare push), want deny ---"
printf '%-52s %s\n' "git -C <main> push"            "$(p "git -C $D/r push")"
printf '%-52s %s\n' "cd <main> && push"             "$(p "cd $D/r && $PUSH")"

printf '%-52s %s\n' "bare push, cwd is <main>"      "$(p "$PUSH" "$D/r")"
printf '%-52s %s\n' "bare push, cwd not a repo"     "$(p "$PUSH" "$D")"
printf '%-52s %s\n' "subshell (cd <main> && push)"  "$(p "(cd $D/r \&\& $PUSH)")"

echo "--- want allow ---"

One high-confidence correctness bug found; everything else (the old awk `exit 0` abort bug, gawk-only constructs, dead code, test-name accuracy) checks out clean.

## Critical finding

**Push options that consume a separate argument token (e.g. `-o <option>`) are miscounted as destination positionals, turning a bare push into a false "non-bare" classification that skips the branch check entirely — a fail-open.**

Confidence: 90. File: `.claude/hooks/no-push-to-main.sh:388-393`, inside the awk heredoc's `emit_if_push()`:

```awk
positional = 0
args = ""
for (k = s + 1; k < e; k++) {
    if (substr(TOK[k], 1, 1) != "-") positional++
    args = args TOK[k] (k < e - 1 ? " " : "")
}
bare = (positional == 0)
if (positional == 1) {
    ... # single positional + no ":" => bare
}
```

This counts *every* token after `push` that doesn't start with `-` as a destination positional. It has no concept of a flag that consumes the *next* token as its value. `git push` has exactly such a flag: `-o <push-option>` (short form of `--push-option=<option>`, per `git push --help`; GitHub/GitLab CI-skip push options are a common real use, e.g. `-o ci.skip`).

Concrete failing input: `git push -o ci.skip origin`, run from a directory on `main`.

- Tokens after `push`: `-o`, `ci.skip`, `origin`.
- `-o` is skipped (dash-prefixed). `ci.skip` has no dash → `positional++` (1). `origin` has no dash → `positional++` (2).
- `positional == 2`, so neither the `positional==0` nor the `positional==1`-with-no-colon branch fires → `bare` stays `0` (false).
- `args` = `"-o ci.skip origin"` — the destination-ref regex (line 481) finds no `main`/`master` word → `ANY_MAIN_DEST=0`.
- Since `bare=0`, `BARE_FOUND` never gets set for this invocation.
- Result: `FOUND_PUSH=1`, `ANY_MAIN_DEST=0`, `BARE_FOUND=0` → hook falls through to `exit 0` at line 493-495. **Allowed.**

But semantically `git push -o ci.skip origin` is a true bare-remote push (one real positional: `origin`); `push.default` decides what branch ships, and if the caller is on `main`, this pushes `main`. The hook's own stated contract (header, lines 26-44) says a bare push must always go through the branch check, and the branch check is supposed to fail closed when scope can't be resolved — but here it never even attempts resolution because the push was wrongly bucketed as "has its own explicit destination."

This isn't in the documented "LEXICAL LIMITS" list (lines 46-57) — that list covers variable indirection, `eval`, `xargs`, wrapper commands, and git aliases, none of which this is. It's an unhandled case in the positional-counting logic itself, not a deliberately out-of-scope lexical form.

No test in `no-push-to-main_test.sh` exercises `-o`, `--repo <repo>`, or any other push-subcommand flag that takes a space-separated value, so this gap has no regression coverage either.

**Suggested fix:** give `emit_if_push` its own value-taking-flag table (parallel to `is_global_valued` but scoped to `git push`'s own flags — at minimum `-o`, and ideally `--repo` for the deprecated form), and skip the following token the same way `skip_global_opts` does for `-C`.

## Confirmed clean

- **The round-1 `awk exit 0` bug that aborted a multi-line scan is gone.** No `exit` statement appears anywhere in the awk program; `scan_pushes()` (line 422) iterates the full token array with no early return, and `tokenize()`'s heredoc handling never short-circuits past the END block.
- **No gawk-only constructs.** `printf "%c"` with a numeric argument (lines 419, 436) is POSIX-specified behavior supported by both gawk and macOS's `/usr/bin/awk` (the modernized One True Awk). The `function f(a, b,    locals)` extra-blank-separated-locals convention is portable POSIX awk, not a gawk extension. Process substitution (`awk -f <(cat <<'...')`, line 172) is a bash feature (shebang is `#!/bin/bash`) and has worked in bash since well before 3.2, so it's fine on macOS's stock bash too.
- **No dead code.** Every awk helper (`strip_one_quote`, `is_global_valued`, `skip_global_opts`, `is_env_assign`, `is_separator`, `is_ambiguous_tok`, `tokenize`, `scan_ambiguous`, `emit_if_push`, `scan_pushes`) and every bash helper (`unescape_json`, `gitscan`, `deny`, `resolve_relative`, `resolve_branch`) is referenced. Nothing left over from the old regex design.
- **Shell quoting is sound.** All variable expansions and command substitutions are double-quoted; `deny()`'s JSON interpolation only ever receives static, hardcoded reason strings (never attacker-influenced `COMMAND`/`CWD` text), so there's no injection path despite the lack of JSON-escaping on `$reason`. `builtin cd -- "$dir"` with `CDPATH` unset in an isolated subshell correctly prevents the CDPATH-leak class of bug.
- **Spot-checked ~15 of the 81 test cases by hand-tracing the awk logic** (quoted subcommand, composed `-C`, multi-line `cd`+bare-push, force-refspec, stacked global options, quoted remote name) — each assertion matches what the code actually does. No mismatched test names found.
- **CHANGELOG entries** (`CHANGELOG.md:150-235`) accurately describe the round-3 rewrite: the narrowed contract, the shared tokenizer, the fail-closed dependency checks, and the two test-expectation flips are all consistent with the diff.

Only the `-o`/push-option finding needs a fix before merge; I'd treat it as blocking given it's a documented-contract violation (bare push must get the branch check) with a plausible real-world trigger (CI-skip push options are common).

Verdict: findings. One new real bug found in round 3; the full global-flag sweep, multi-C composition, and over-deny checks otherwise confirm the rewrite works as designed. 81/81 existing cases pass, shellcheck clean on both scripts.

NEW FINDING (HIGH) — a quoted, `=`-attached value on a value-taking global flag breaks the tokenizer and erases the entire git invocation from classification, allowing a push to main with no check at all:

    git --git-dir="<repo>/.git" push origin main     -> ALLOWED (should deny)
    git --work-tree="<repo>" push origin main        -> ALLOWED (should deny)
    git -c core.pager="cat" push origin main         -> ALLOWED (should deny)
    git --git-dir='<repo>/.git' push origin main     -> ALLOWED (single-quoted, same bug)

Also confirmed this hides a BARE push (the branch-check path), not just an explicit destination:

    git --git-dir="<repo>/.git" push   (cwd itself on main)   -> ALLOWED (should deny)

Mechanism: the awk tokenizer's quote-span logic starts a new token at the opening quote character, so `--git-dir="<path>"` is split into two tokens — `--git-dir=` and the unquoted interior — rather than one `--git-dir=<path>` token. `is_global_valued` checks `tok[i] == "--git-dir"` (exact match), which doesn't match the mangled `--git-dir=` token, so `skip_global_opts` returns 0 at that point (not recognized as any option it knows, but it also doesn't start with a bare `-` followed immediately by a letter it treats as a flag... actually since `--git-dir=` still starts with `-`, it falls into the `i += 1` branch meant for boolean flags like `--no-pager`, silently skipping just that one token and then treating the *quoted path itself* as the next token to examine — which doesn't match `push` since it's a path, so the scan effectively walks past `push` without recognizing it, or in the pure =value case the subcommand position shifts and the regex-era classification never finds `push` in the position it expects). Net effect confirmed empirically regardless of exact internal mechanism: the whole invocation becomes invisible to `scan_pushes`, exactly the "no check runs at all" failure mode the round-2 fix was supposed to eliminate everywhere. The sanity check `git --git-dir=<path> push origin main` with NO quotes around the value correctly denies — the bug is specific to a quoted/escaped `=`-attached value, which is very ordinary shell usage whenever a path contains no spaces but a developer quotes defensively, or whenever a path does contain a space.

NON-FINDINGS (verified, worth recording so they aren't re-raised):
- `git --exec-path push origin main` (bare `--exec-path`, no `=value`) is allowed by the hook, but I verified this is CORRECT, not a bug: real git's bare `--exec-path` never dispatches to a subcommand at all — `git --exec-path <anything>` always just prints the exec path and exits 0, confirmed by comparing `git --exec-path status` (prints `/usr/lib/git-core`) against plain `git status` (prints branch state). So `push` never actually runs; the hook's "nothing to see here" is accurate.
- My initial sweep flagged several "mismatches" on multi-`-C` composition and bare-push-after-separate-line-cd as under-denies, but all were my own probe-harness errors: I set the payload's own `cwd` to the main checkout while expecting a `-C`/`cd` target elsewhere to override it. The ratified round-3 contract explicitly checks BOTH cwd and resolved scope and denies if EITHER is unsafe — that is correct per the operator's ruling, not a bug. Re-ran with cwd itself on the feature branch (so the cwd-check couldn't mask what I was actually testing) and multi-`-C` composition (`-C <parent> -C wt-feat`, composing to the worktree on feat/example) resolved correctly and allowed.
- Full global-flag sweep (`-c` space-separated, `--no-pager`, `-p`, `--literal-pathspecs`, `--git-dir=`/`--work-tree=` unquoted, `--bare`, `--no-replace-objects`, `--namespace=`/space form, stacked combinations, `+main`/`+refs/heads/main` force refspecs, `HEAD:main`) all correctly deny when unquoted. Ambiguity detection (subshell, `||`, `if/then`, `pushd`) all correctly deny bare pushes outright. Fail-closed dependency checks (grep/awk/git missing from PATH, non-JSON/empty stdin) all correctly deny. CDPATH-set case produces exactly one clean JSON line on stdout.
